Full affinity ownership and recovery remain unfinished. Checkpoint 5 percent-encodes non-ASCII UTF-8 upstream base-path bytes before native dispatch, preserving existing percent escapes, combining sequences and Chat Completions query forwarding; eight path/route cases match the pinned production release. Checkpoint 6 selects the frozen unscoped history context for native Super while retaining scoped internal relays; equal comma-list HTTP lengths and first-present tool-ID mapping match focused 0.439.1 production checks. Binding ownership remains a visible mismatch. Checkpoint 7 applies the existing ASCII response-header validation to buffered passthrough, matching the pinned TinyHTTP constructor without altering binary bodies or replaying requests. Checkpoint 8 resolves the first nonblank explicit session-header alias before metadata/body fallback, with six live 0.439.1 vectors and zero POSTs for oversized resolved identities. Checkpoint 9 extends the existing upstream path byte encoder to quotes, angle brackets, backticks and braces, preserving existing percent escapes and tested unescaped punctuation. The timeout and aggregate-state worker proposals are excluded; broader transport and resource parity remains unqualified. Checkpoint 10 converts admitted base-path backslashes to HTTP URL separators after literal trailing-slash trimming, preserving repeated separators and encoded backslashes in twelve live path/route vectors. Dot-segment normalization remains unsupported and denied by the existing guard.
blockers: The production slice requires a clean base and explicit loopback/model/key/options. Complete provider preset routing and custom catalog/config options, real Codex distributions, native Messages, account rotation, TLS and general provider launch remain unverified or unfinished.
